title: Tag Registry
content_html:
Tag Registry

Capability

/studio/tag-registry/ maintains canonical tags: browse/filter, create, edit, delete, and demote a tag into an alias.

Canonical identity has wider consequences than visible registry rows. Rename/delete/demotion can affect aliases and assignments, so the server planners own impact calculation and cross-file mutation.

Workflow

load registry + aliases + assignments
  -> filter/search or open mutation modal
  -> validate candidate ID/group/description
  -> preview destructive or cross-file impact
  -> confirm
  -> server planner + atomic apply
  -> reload canonical data + activity evidence

When the Local Studio tag service is unavailable, supported simple operations produce manual JSON patch guidance. That is a fallback handoff, not a canonical write or guaranteed multi-file transaction.

New Tag sends {tag_id, group, description} to the focused /create-tag operation. The server validates the flat ID and scalar group independently, rejects invalid or duplicate identity before writing, owns timestamps, atomically appends one row, and records create-tag activity. Server validation failures stay in the create workflow; only service unavailability switches creation to manual patch mode.

Edit keeps tag_id readonly in the normal route while allowing the scalar group and description to change independently. A group change validates every affected alias constraint before the registry write.

The route displays tag_id directly; canonical rows do not have a separate label. The Edit Tag modal uses the tag ID as its heading and exposes the four group pills as a single-choice control. It has no disabled identity field or duplicate current-group badge.

Durable Rules

  • canonical IDs are globally unique slug-safe names;
  • registry rows use tag_registry_v3 and contain no label; tag_id is both identity and displayed tag name;
  • every tag has exactly one allowed scalar group, which is not part of the ID;
  • ordinary creation has its own single-record planner and API rather than registry-import semantics;
  • deletion and demotion must account for alias/assignment references;
  • demotion replaces a canonical tag with an alias targeting selected remaining canonical tags;
  • local-server mutations record one initiating action context in Admin activity.

Exact limits, request shapes, and effect payloads live in tag_source_model.py, focused planners, and tests.

Code Map

  • template/controller: tag-registry.html, tag-registry.js
  • state/render/modal/save modules: studio/app/frontend/js/tag-registry-*
  • HTTP boundary: studio/app/server/studio/studio_tag_api/registry.py, studio_tag_api/promotions.py
  • planners: studio/services/tags/tag_registry_mutations.py, tag_promotion_mutations.py
  • canonical source: studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-registry.json

The route root follows the shared Studio ready/busy contract. Mutation modal state is route mode; service availability reflects direct-write capability.

Weak Spots And Change Method

  • Manual patch fallback cannot safely reproduce every cross-file server mutation; keep its supported surface explicit.
  • The controller remains a large coordinator even after state/render/workflow modules were split.
  • Visible copy is code-owned in tag-ui-text.js, so it can drift from server terminology.

Change the domain planner and tests before the modal/controller. Add UI detail here only when it reveals a durable workflow or ownership boundary.
